comment: This is a rewrite rather than a port: src/velamina.cpp implements the revised Veils behaviour directly on Rack's SIMD accessors, and the maker cites the gain curve graph the hardware manual points at. The signal jacks are left without a family because an amplifier carries whatever you patch into it. The gain is worked out two different ways: with a cable at the channel's CV jack, velamina.cpp:119 computes the CV times the slider plus the offset, clamps that to 0..8, divides by 5 and raises it to a power set by the response knob; with no cable, velamina.cpp:123 uses the slider plus the offset with no division at all, so the offset knob's 5V worth of range is added straight to a gain of at most 1 and the channel can reach a gain of six. The manual says the offset applies to the modulation and not to the signal, which holds only while a CV cable is present. The chaining is done by clearing the running sum only when a channel's output is connected, at velamina.cpp:141.
